headline: Pentanet lifts FY26 earnings expectations by 74% to $2.4M as cloud gaming subscribers migrate to higher-tier plans amid GPU and AI tailwinds
reasoning: Pentanet's unaudited FY26 results show group revenue up 8% from the prior corresponding period and earnings expectations lifted 74% to $2.4 million. CEO Stephen Cornish attributes the improved performance to cloud gaming subscribers migrating to higher-tier subscription plans, driven by GPU and memory shortages as the industry pivots toward AI, which is creating tailwinds for Pentanet's cloud gaming business. Pentanet is the exclusive provider of Nvidia's GeForce Now platform in Australia and New Zealand, owning a large cluster of Nvidia GPUs that render games in the cloud, allowing consumers to access high-end gaming on any device via a subscription rather than purchasing expensive hardware. Cornish notes that as GPU hardware prices continue rising due to data centre demand, Pentanet's cloud gaming value proposition becomes more compelling for consumers. The company is also conducting a strategic review of its business units — telecommunications and the Nvidia cloud gaming business — to determine where to focus capital for the best returns over the next five years, including potentially finding ways to generate additional revenue from its existing GPU infrastructure beyond gaming.
quote: A lot of our cloud gaming subscribers are starting to migrate and move on to the higher tier plans. Um, that's due to the things happening in the industry around memory and GPU shortages, and everything's sort of skewing and moving to AI, which is creating some nice tailwinds for our cloud gaming business, which we've been heavily involved in for several years now... Our North Star still as a business, is to use and run these GPUs for gaming, and that's what we do. We've got the moat around that business and that's a huge market to come. But as we get further down the line, you know, as a company, we'll be looking to do smart things and where to, you know, fill in more revenue onto this existing infrastructure.
episode_title: Nvidia partnership boosts this small cap's earnings

headline: Pentanet CEO outlines GPU cloud gaming strategy and telecom growth as key value drivers ahead of strategic review release
reasoning: Stephen Cornish describes Pentanet's core business as running high-end data centre GPUs for cloud gaming, which he sees as the company's primary moat and a large addressable market. The telco business in Perth provides a stable, predictable revenue base growing around 8% year-on-year with low churn, and supports the infrastructure economics. The company is at an inflection point competing with NBN, but retains local service and brand advantages to improve ARPU. Cornish sees significant unrealised value in the company and expects upcoming full-year results and the release of a strategic review to be the next key share price catalysts.
quote: Our North Star still as a business, is to use and run these GPUs for gaming, and that's what we do. We've got the moat around that business and that's a huge market to come. But as we get further down the line, you know, as a company, we'll be looking to do smart things and where to, you know, fill in more revenue onto this existing infrastructure... I think the next catalysts for the share price would just be, you know, probably the market responding and seeing probably what I would see is a huge amount of value still sitting on the table with where we are today and what we can do moving forward and and executing on that strategy.
episode_title: Nvidia partnership boosts this small cap's earnings
